newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's SBAB warns of tough housing loans market.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's SBAB warns of tough housing loans market.

text.p: The Swedish National Housing Finance Corp, SBAB, on Thursday posted net operating income of 572 million crowns for 1996 compared with 516 million a year earlier but warned that competition has got tougher.
"During 1996 competition has stiffened still further, leading to sharply reduced margins," SBAB said in a statement.

"If this competitive situation continues, the result will be that very large volumes of loans with good margins will be renewed at much narrower margins, resulting in reduced profitability for the housing mortgage institutions."
SBAB, which is owned by Sweden's Finance Ministry, said the sharp fall in interest rates, which reduced return on flows and equity capital, played a large part in this profitability squeeze.

SBAB said the improvement in 1996 was greater than indicated by the comparative 1995 figure as SBAB in 1995 received payments under the capital adequacy guarantee amounting to 1.0 billion crowns for the portfolio of government-agency approved loans.
"The actual improvement in operating income in 1996 thus amounts to more than 1.0 billion crowns," SBAB said in a statement.
It said its loan portfolio has been greatly improved as a result of the transaction with the government in 1995.
Loan losses in 1996 fell to 318 million crowns in 1996 compared to 1.64 billion crowns in 1995.
Lending in 1996 decreased by 1.75 billion crowns to 135.18 billion crowns.
"The whole of SBAB's loan portfolio is now adapted to market conditions, exposed to competition and credit-approved by the company," SBAB said.

"This provides SBAB with the conditions required to carry out the task identified for SBAB by parliament and the government: to promote competition and diversity in Sweden's housing mortgage market by operating effectively and profitably."
